reason: No universal arbitrary-multiplicity exponential theorem is claimed or supplied. The fixed-M bound has c_M=1/(M+1/log2), tending to zero, so it cannot yield one c>0 for all occurrence multisets. The same-constant threshold removal and equivalence with logarithmic-mass assertion(L) transfer the central difficulty to an expressly unproved equivalent assertion. The example bounds only constants above(30/59)log15 and does not refute existence of a smaller positive c. Korsky's credited stretched-exponential claim is weaker and is not used as an accepted dependency.
